claim: ESCRTs constitute hetero-oligomeric machines that catalyze multiple topologically similar membrane-remodeling processes.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) constitute hetero-oligomeric machines that catalyze multiple topologically similar membrane-remodeling processes.
evidence: This is a general characterization of ESCRT function stated in the abstract.

claim: ESCRT-III subunits polymerize into spirals.
source: Although ESCRT-III subunits polymerize into spirals, how individual ESCRT-III subunits are activated and assembled together into a membrane-deforming filament remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: X-ray crystal structures of Snf7 in its active conformation were determined.
source: Here, we determine X-ray crystal structures of the most abundant ESCRT-III subunit Snf7 in its active conformation.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by crystallographic data in Table 1.

claim: Snf7 activation requires a prominent conformational rearrangement to expose protein-membrane and protein-protein interfaces.
source: Using pulsed dipolar electron spin resonance spectroscopy (PDS), we show that Snf7 activation requires a prominent conformational rearrangement to expose protein-membrane and protein-protein interfaces.
evidence: This is supported by PDS experimental data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Snf7 arrays assemble with ~30 Å periodicity into a membrane-sculpting filament.
source: This promotes the assembly of Snf7 arrays with ~30 Å periodicity into a membrane-sculpting filament.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data and PDS measurements shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mutations on protein interfaces halt Snf7 assembly and block ESCRT function both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Using a combination of biochemical and genetic approaches, both in vitro and in vivo, we demonstrate that mutations on these protein interfaces halt Snf7 assembly and block ESCRT function.
evidence: This is supported by MVB sorting assays and TEM data shown in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: ESCRTs mediate the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) are membrane remodeling machinery that mediate diverse fundamental cellular processes, including the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation (Katzmann et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRTs mediate enveloped virus budding.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) are membrane remodeling machinery that mediate diverse fundamental cellular processes, including the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation (Katzmann et al., 2001), enveloped virus budding (Garrus et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRTs mediate cytokinesis.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) are membrane remodeling machinery that mediate diverse fundamental cellular processes, including the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation (Katzmann et al., 2001), enveloped virus budding (Garrus et al., 2001), cytokinesis (Carlton and Martin-Serrano, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRTs mediate plasma membrane repair.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) are membrane remodeling machinery that mediate diverse fundamental cellular processes, including the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation (Katzmann et al., 2001), enveloped virus budding (Garrus et al., 2001), cytokinesis (Carlton and Martin-Serrano, 2007), plasma membrane repair (Jimenez et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRTs mediate nuclear pore complex assembly.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) are membrane remodeling machinery that mediate diverse fundamental cellular processes, including the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation (Katzmann et al., 2001), enveloped virus budding (Garrus et al., 2001), cytokinesis (Carlton and Martin-Serrano, 2007), plasma membrane repair (Jimenez et al., 2014), nuclear pore complex assembly (Webster et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRTs mediate nuclear envelope reformation.
source: The endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) are membrane remodeling machinery that mediate diverse fundamental cellular processes, including the biogenesis of multivesicular body (MVB) during receptor down-regulation (Katzmann et al., 2001), enveloped virus budding (Garrus et al., 2001), cytokinesis (Carlton and Martin-Serrano, 2007), plasma membrane repair (Jimenez et al., 2014), nuclear pore complex assembly (Webster et al., 2014), and nuclear envelope reformation (Olmos et al., 2015; Vietri et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRTs were originally identified using yeast genetics.
source: Originally identified using yeast genetics, ESCRTs package ubiquitinated transmembrane proteins into intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) that bud into the interior of the late endosome, creating a MVB that ultimately delivers cargos into the yeast lysosome (vacuole).
evidence: This is stated as historical context based on established knowledge.

claim: ESCRTs package ubiquitinated transmembrane proteins into intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) that bud into the interior of the late endosome.
source: Originally identified using yeast genetics, ESCRTs package ubiquitinated transmembrane proteins into intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) that bud into the interior of the late endosome, creating a MVB that ultimately delivers cargos into the yeast lysosome (vacuole).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ESCRT function.

claim: Upstream ESCRT components (ESCRTs-0, I, and II) assemble into stable hetero-multimers to sort ubiquitinated cargo on the endosomal surface.
source: Upstream ESCRT components, ESCRTs-0, I, and II, assemble into stable hetero-multimers to sort ubiquitinated cargo on the endosomal surface by binding ubiquitin and endosomal lipid, phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI(3)P).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ESCRT pathway function.

claim: ESCRT-II sets the architecture and initiates the assembly of the ESCRT-III complex.
source: In addition, ESCRT-II sets the architecture and initiates the assembly of the ESCRT-III complex, which together with Vps4 is responsible for remodeling endosomal membranes (Henne et al., 2011; Hurley and Hanson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III together with Vps4 is responsible for remodeling endosomal membranes.
source: In addition, ESCRT-II sets the architecture and initiates the assembly of the ESCRT-III complex, which together with Vps4 is responsible for remodeling endosomal membranes (Henne et al., 2011; Hurley and Hanson, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III is a metastable and conformationally dynamic protein complex.
source: ESCRT-III is a unique protein complex in that it is metastable and conformationally dynamic, forming hetero-oligomeric filaments of multiple subunits on membranes (Saksena et al., 2009; Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III forms hetero-oligomeric filaments of multiple subunits on membranes.
source: ESCRT-III is a unique protein complex in that it is metastable and conformationally dynamic, forming hetero-oligomeric filaments of multiple subunits on membranes (Saksena et al., 2009; Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III subunits are inactive monomers in the cytoplasm.
source: Its subunits are inactive monomers in the cytoplasm, which activate and assemble into spiraling polymers on endosomes to drive cargo sequestration, membrane invagination and constriction (Buchkovich et al., 2013; Hanson et al., 2008; Henne et al., 2012; Wollert and Hurley, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III subunits activate and assemble into spiraling polymers on endosomes to drive cargo sequestration, membrane invagination and constriction.
source: Its subunits are inactive monomers in the cytoplasm, which activate and assemble into spiraling polymers on endosomes to drive cargo sequestration, membrane invagination and constriction (Buchkovich et al., 2013; Hanson et al., 2008; Henne et al., 2012; Wollert and Hurley, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III is a hetero-polymer of four 'core' subunits: Vps20, Snf7/Vps32, Vps24 and Vps2.
source: ESCRT-III is a hetero-polymer of four "core' subunits of Vps20, Snf7/Vps32, Vps24 and Vps2 (Babst et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III has 'accessory' subunits including Ist1, Did2/Vps46, Vps60, and Chm7.
source: ESCRT-III is a hetero-polymer of four "core' subunits of Vps20, Snf7/Vps32, Vps24 and Vps2 (Babst et al., 2002), and 'accessory' subunits of Ist1, Did2/Vps46, Vps60 (Rue et al., 2008) and Chm7 (Horii et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-II directly engages Vps20 to trigger a sequential activation and ordered assembly of ESCRT-III subunits at endosomes.
source: ESCRT-II directly engages Vps20 to trigger a sequential activation and ordered assembly of ESCRT-III subunits at endosomes (Teis et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Vps20 nucleates the homo-oligomerization of Snf7.
source: Vps20 nucleates the homo-oligomerization of the most abundant ESCRT-III subunit, Snf7, which then recruits Vps24 and Vps2 (Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Snf7 recruits Vps24 and Vps2.
source: Vps20 nucleates the homo-oligomerization of the most abundant ESCRT-III subunit, Snf7, which then recruits Vps24 and Vps2 (Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Vps2 engages the Vps4 complex for ESCRT-III disassembly.
source: Vps2 finally engages the Vps4 complex for ESCRT-III disassembly (Lata et al., 2008b; Obita et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-mediated membrane remodeling produces membrane curvature that pushes away from the cytoplasm.
source: ESCRT-mediated membrane remodeling produces membrane curvature that pushes away from the cytoplasm, which is topologically opposite to that of the 'classical' clathrin and COP-I/II vesicle budding reactions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ESCRT function.

claim: ESCRT-mediated membrane curvature is topologically opposite to that of clathrin and COP-I/II vesicle budding reactions.
source: ESCRT-mediated membrane remodeling produces membrane curvature that pushes away from the cytoplasm, which is topologically opposite to that of the 'classical' clathrin and COP-I/II vesicle budding reactions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge comparing ESCRT to other membrane remodeling systems.

claim: High-resolution structural studies of ESCRT-III polymers have been problematic due to their relative instability and heterogeneity.
source: However, due to the relative instability and heterogeneity of ESCRT-III polymers, high-resolution structural studies have generally been problematic.
evidence: This is stated as a challenge in the field based on the nature of ESCRT-III.

claim: Structural work on Snf7 has been difficult due to its ability to assemble readily into polymers that interfere with crystallization.
source: Structural work on Snf7 in particular has been difficult, due to its ability to assemble readily into polymers that interfere with crystallization.
evidence: This is stated as a technical challenge specific to Snf7 structural studies.

claim: Snf7 contains a highly structured 'core' domain of four α-helices.
source: Snf7 contains a highly structured 'core' domain of four α-helices (Muziol et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The C-terminus of Snf7 includes an α-helix (α5) that folds back against the core domain in cis to mediate autoinhibition.
source: The C-terminus, in contrast, is less structured, including an α-helix (α5) that folds back against the core domain in cis to mediate autoinhibition (Lata et al., 2008a)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The C-terminus of Snf7 includes a MIT-interacting motif (MIM) for Vps4 recognition.
source: The C-terminus, in contrast, is less structured, including an α-helix (α5) that folds back against the core domain in cis to mediate autoinhibition (Lata et al., 2008a), a microtubule interacting and transport (MIT)-interacting motif (MIM) for Vps4 recognition (Obita et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The C-terminus of Snf7 includes an α-helix (α6) for Bro1/Alix interaction.
source: The C-terminus, in contrast, is less structured, including an α-helix (α5) that folds back against the core domain in cis to mediate autoinhibition (Lata et al., 2008a), a microtubule interacting and transport (MIT)-interacting motif (MIM) for Vps4 recognition (Obita et al., 2007), and an α-helix (α6) for Bro1/Alix interaction (McCullough et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: ESCRT-III subunits are activated by intramolecular conformational changes that promote protein-protein interactions.
source: Numerous studies indicate that ESCRT-III subunits are activated by intramolecular conformational changes that promote protein-protein interactions (Henne et al., 2012; Lata et al., 2008a; Saksena et al., 2009; Schuh et al., 2015; Shen et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: Available X-ray crystal structures of autoinhibited Vps24 and Ist1 suggest that conformational changes involve the disruption of intramolecular interactions between the basic N-terminus and the acidic C-terminus.
source: Available X-ray crystal structures of the autoinhibited Vps24 (Muziol et al., 2006) and Ist1 (Bajorek et al., 2009; Xiao et al., 2009) suggest that these conformational changes involve the disruption of intramolecular interactions between the basic N-terminus and the acidic C-terminus.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited crystal structures.

claim: Upon releasing autoinhibition, Snf7 subunits assemble into higher-order protofilaments or spirals.
source: Upon releasing this autoinhibition, Snf7 subunits assemble into higher-order protofilaments or spirals (Cashikar et al., 2014; Hanson et al., 2008; Henne et al., 2012; Shen et al., 2014) with a range of different morphologies and dimensions.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Snf7core was crystallized and structures were solved at 1.6 Å and 2.4 Å resolutions.
source: We then crystallized and solved X-ray crystal structures of Snf7core in two conformations at 1.6 Å and 2.4 Å resolutions, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary experimental result supported by crystallographic data in Table 1.

claim: The Snf7core structures were determined by molecular replacement using CHMP4Bα1-α2 (PDB: 4ABM).
source: The structures were determined by molecular replacement using CHMP4Bα1-α2 (PDB: 4ABM) (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the method used for structure determination.

claim: Snf7core does not fold into four α-helices, but instead contains only three α-helices that pack into a highly elongated structure.
source: When we superimposed our Snf7 structure with available ESCRT-III structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), we were surprised to note that Snf7core does not fold into four α-helices, but instead, it contains only three α-helices that pack into a highly elongated structure (Figures 1B–C).
evidence: This is a primary structural finding from the crystal structure.

claim: In Snf7core, α2 extends into a ~90 Å long α-helix combining the α2 and α3 segments.
source: α2 extends into a ~90 Å long α-helix combining the α2 and α3 segments that were distinct α-helices in previously defined ESCRT-III structures (Figures 2A–B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In the closed state, Gln90 (α2) and Met130 (α4) of Snf7 are in close proximity.
source: Using a homology model of closed Snf7 (Henne et al., 2012) (Figure 2A), we identified close proximity between conserved residues Gln90 (α2) and Met130 (α4) in the four-helix coiled-coil (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of a homology model.

claim: In the S13 (cytoplasmic) fraction, ~50% of Snf7Q90C M130C migrated faster after oxidation, indicating a conformationally closed Snf7 species.
source: Strikingly, in the S13 fraction, ~50% of Snf7Q90C M130C migrated faster, indicating a conformationally closed Snf7 species.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the crosslinking assay shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the P13 (membrane-enriched) fraction, the migration shift of Snf7Q90C M130C did not occur after oxidation.
source: Notably, in the P13 fraction, the migration shift did not occur (Figures 2D–E).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the crosslinking assay shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Snf7 on endosomal membranes adopts an open conformation in which α4 is displaced away from α2.
source: This is indicative of distinct conformations between the cytoplasmic and the endosome-bound states, and suggests that Snf7 on endosomal membranes adopts an open conformation in which α4 is displaced away from α2.
evidence: This is an inference from the crosslinking data in Figure 2D.

claim: Soluble Snf7 is structurally heterogeneous and conformationally dynamic.
source: The result showed a wide distance spread of ~15–50 Å (Figure 2I), corresponding to large amplitude motions of the spin labeled positions, but not a distinct closed or open state. Thus, soluble Snf7 is structurally heterogeneous, suggesting that it is conformationally dynamic (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation of DEER spectroscopy data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Membrane-bound Snf7R52E E88C H118C produced a strong ~30 Å peak in DEER measurements.
source: Intriguingly, membrane-bound Snf7R52E E88C H118C produced a strong ~30 Å peak.
evidence: This is an experimental result from DEER spectroscopy shown in Figure 2K.

claim: Only the open conformation is present in Snf7 polymers assembled on membranes.
source: As we did not observe short distances corresponding to the closed conformation, we conclude that only the open conformation is present in Snf7 polymers assembled on membranes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on DEER spectroscopy data.

claim: Each Snf7 protomer in the crystal lattice exhibits a repeat distance of ~30 Å.
source: Each of the ~100 Å long α1–3 hairpin tilts by ~27° and polymerizes into a ~45 Å diameter single protofilament, with each protomer exhibiting a repeat distance of ~30 Å (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure shown in Figure 3A.

claim: DEER measurements on single-labeled Snf7 showed moderately broad distance distributions at 28–32 Å for T20C, K35C and E88C.
source: Consistent with the extensive amount of inter-molecular contacts revealed in the Snf7 crystal, we observed moderately broad distance distributions, specifically at 28–32 Å for T20C, K35C and E88C (Figures 3B–C)
evidence: This is an experimental result from DEER spectroscopy shown in Figure 3B.

claim: DEER measurements on single-labeled Snf7 showed moderately broad distance distributions at 32–36 Å for K60C, H118C and G140C.
source: Consistent with the extensive amount of inter-molecular contacts revealed in the Snf7 crystal, we observed moderately broad distance distributions, specifically at 28–32 Å for T20C, K35C and E88C (Figures 3B–C), and at 32–36 Å for K60C, H118C and G140C (Figures 3D–E).
evidence: This is an experimental result from DEER spectroscopy shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Snf7 packing adopts a parallel arrangement in a single-layer array with a period of ~30 Å.
source: Based on this series of single-cysteine DEER scanning and the double-cysteine magnetic dilution experiments, we conclude that Snf7 packing adopts a parallel arrangement in a single-layer array with a period of ~30 Å
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple DEER experiments.

claim: In the Snf7 protofilament, protomer (i) interacts with protomer (i+1) through both hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions.
source: In the Snf7 protofilament, the protomer (i) interacts with the next protomer (i+1) through both hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions (Figures 4A–B), burying ~1060 Å2 of solvent-accessible surface area per protomer.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure shown in Figure 4.

claim: The assembly of the extended α2/3 helix exposes a hydrophobic surface on α3 that was buried in the closed state.
source: The assembly of the extended α2/3 helix exposes a hydrophobic surface on α3, which was buried in the closed state.
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing open and closed conformations.

claim: Snf7 mutants M104E, L101E, A97K, I94E, Q90K, M87E and T83E showed severe MVB sorting defects with sorting efficiencies from 12% to 76%.
source: As a result, mutants M104E, L101E, A97K, I94E, Q90K, M87E and T83E showed severe sorting defects, with sorting efficiencies from 12% to 76%
evidence: This is an experimental result from the MVB sorting assay shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Snf7 mutants L121D, I117E, M114E, M107E, T103E and L99K showed MVB sorting defects with sorting efficiencies from 7% to 34%.
source: As a result, mutants M104E, L101E, A97K, I94E, Q90K, M87E and T83E showed severe sorting defects, with sorting efficiencies from 12% to 76%, and mutants L121D, I117E, M114E, M107E, T103E and L99K from 7% to 34% (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the MVB sorting assay shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Recombinant Snf7R52E Q90K, Snf7R52E I94E, Snf7R52E M107E, and Snf7R52E M114E proteins were unable to generate protofilaments visible by TEM.
source: Furthermore, recombinant Snf7R52E Q90K, Snf7R52E I94E, Snf7R52E M107E, and Snf7R52E M114E proteins were able to be purified to homogeneity, but unable to generate protofilaments visible by TEM (Figure 4H and Figure 4— figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental result from TEM analysis shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Snf7 mutants snf7R25E H29E K36E and snf7E95K E102K E109K resulted in severe MVB sorting defects of 16% and 44%, respectively.
source: To validate whether these inter-protomer electrostatic interactions occur in vivo, we generated and tested charge-inversion mutations, snf7R25E H29E K36E and snf7E95K E102K E109K, which resulted in severe sorting defects of 16% and 44%, respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the MVB sorting assay shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Co-expressing snf7R25E H29E K36E and snf7E95K E102K E109K in trans restored MVB sorting to 91%.
source: Strikingly, when co-expressing both mutants in trans, MVB sorting was restored to 91% (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the MVB sorting assay shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Co-incubating recombinant Snf7R52E R25E H29E K36E and Snf7R52E E95K E102K E109K proteins resulted in protofilament formation.
source: Furthermore, co-incubating recombinant Snf7R52E R25E H29E K36E and Snf7R52E E95K E102K E109K proteins resulted in protofilament formation, but no protofilaments were detected when each mutant was tested individually (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is an experimental result from TEM analysis shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Key conserved lysine residues K60 K64 K68 K71 K79 (α2), and K112 K115 (α3) are arranged on an elongated and solvent-exposed surface ideal for interacting with the acidic endosomal membrane.
source: Strikingly, several key conserved lysine residues, K60 K64 K68 K71 K79 (α2), and K112 K115 (α3), which were in distinct α-helices in the closed state, are arranged on an elongated and solvent-exposed surface ideal for interacting with the acidic endosomal membrane.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure related to membrane binding.

claim: The electrostatic membrane-binding regions of all Snf7 protomers face the same direction in the polymer.
source: The electrostatic membrane-binding regions of all Snf7 protomers face the same direction in the polymer, allowing for a continuous membrane-binding interface (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure shown in Figure 5B.

claim: α4 can rotate by at least ~90° along the axis of the α2/3 helix between the two open conformations.
source: Superimposing the two conformations revealed that α4 can rotate by at least ~90° along the axis of the α2/3 helix (Figures 6A–B).
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing the two crystal structures shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: α4 makes a similar interaction with the α1/2 hairpin of a Snf7 protomer in a neighboring protofilament in both open conformations.
source: Despite the large differences in α4 positioning, α4 makes a similar interaction with the α1/2 hairpin of a Snf7 protomer in a neighboring protofilament in both structures (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a structural observation from both crystal structures.

claim: Snf7 mutants A51E, L55E, L67E, V126E, M130E and I133E led to drastic loss-of-function with sorting efficiencies from 9% to 55% in vivo.
source: Snf7 mutants of A51E, L55E, L67E, V126E, M130E and I133E led to drastic loss-of-function, with sorting efficiencies from 9% to 55% in vivo, and were unable to assemble into protofilaments in vitro (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the MVB sorting assay shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Snf7 mutants A51E, L55E, L67E, V126E, M130E and I133E were unable to assemble into protofilaments in vitro.
source: Snf7 mutants of A51E, L55E, L67E, V126E, M130E and I133E led to drastic loss-of-function, with sorting efficiencies from 9% to 55% in vivo, and were unable to assemble into protofilaments in vitro (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from TEM analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The L121P mutant exhibited a MVB sorting efficiency of 32%.
source: The L121P mutant exhibited a MVB sorting efficiency of 32%, compared to that of the α1/2 loop residue Asn59 mutant N59P of 75% (Figure 6— figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is an experimental result from the MVB sorting assay shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Seven highly conserved regions were identified in the Snf7core domain by CONSURF analysis.
source: As a result, we identified seven highly conserved regions in the Snf7core domain (Figure 7A and Figure 7— figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from CONSURF sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: All seven highly conserved regions in Snf7core map to regions assigned specific functions in either polymer assembly or membrane interaction.
source: Strikingly, all of them map to regions of Snf7 assigned specific functions in either polymer assembly or membrane interaction
evidence: This is an observation connecting conservation analysis to functional regions.

claim: A linear Snf7 filament can bend into a ~70 nm diameter three-dimensional superhelix with turn length of ~62 nm using normal mode analysis.
source: Remarkably, without any dramatic structural rearrangement within each protomer or alterations of the protein-protein interface, a linear two-dimensional Snf7 filament can bend into a ~70 nm diameter three-dimensional superhelix with turn length of ~62 nm, reminiscent of the structure of the Snf7/Vps24/Vps2 co-assembly previously observed (Henne et al., 2012) (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from normal mode analysis computational modeling shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: The 3D helical Snf7 array aligns the cationic membrane-binding surfaces on the outside of the superhelix.
source: Importantly, this 3D helical array aligns the cationic membrane-binding surfaces on the outside of the superhelix, ideal for a Snf7 polymer to stabilize a negatively curved membrane surface (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is an observation from the normal mode analysis model shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Snf7 intermolecular interactions rely primarily on core-core and core-membrane interactions.
source: Because Snf7 intermolecular interactions rely primarily on core-core and core-membrane interactions (Figure 1A) (Buchkovich et al., 2013; Henne et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Snf7core (residues 12–150) was purified to homogeneity.
source: we purified Snf7core to homogeneity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Snf7core conformation A was crystallized in 100 mM NaCl, 100 mM MES:NaOH pH5.5, 3% PEG20,000.
source: Snf7core (conformation A) was crystallized in a hanging-drop vapor diffusion system at 4°C by mixing protein (5.7 mg/mL) with reservoir solution containing 100 mM NaCl, 100 mM MES:NaOH pH5.5, 3% PEG20,000 in 1:1 ratio (v/v).
evidence: This describes the crystallization conditions used.

claim: Snf7core conformation B crystals were grown in 110 mM NaCl, 70 mM MES:NaOH pH5.5, 6% PEG20,000 and subject to high-pressure cryo-cooling.
source: Snf7core (conformation B) crystals were grown in 110 mM NaCl, 70 mM MES:NaOH pH5.5, 6% PEG20,000 and subject to high-pressure cryo-cooling (Kim et al., 2005).
evidence: This describes the crystallization and cryo-cooling conditions used.

claim: X-ray diffraction data for Snf7 crystal A was collected to 2.4 Å at MacCHESS beam line F1.
source: X-ray diffraction data was collected on Snf7 crystal 'A' to 2.4 Å at MacCHESS beam line F1 of Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source.
evidence: This describes the data collection method.

claim: Snf7 crystal A belonged to space group P21 with unit cell dimensions a=29.5 Å b=52.2 Å c=54.5 Å α=90° β=97.5° γ=90°.
source: The crystal belonged to space group P21 with unit cell dimensions a=29.5 Å b=52.2 Å c=54.5 Å α=90° β=97.5° γ=90°.
evidence: This is crystallographic data from the structure determination.

claim: X-ray diffraction data for Snf7 crystal B was collected to 1.6 Å.
source: X-ray diffraction data was collected on crystal 'B' to 1.6 Å.
evidence: This describes the data collection resolution.

claim: Snf7 crystal B belonged to space group P21 with unit cell dimensions a=29.9 Å b=46.2 Å c=44.6 Å α=90° β=98.5° γ=90°.
source: It belonged to space group P21 with unit cell dimensions a=29.9 Å b=46.2 Å c=44.6 Å α=90° β=98.5° γ=90°.
evidence: This is crystallographic data from the structure determination.

claim: There is one Snf7 molecule in the asymmetric unit of both crystals.
source: There is one Snf7 molecule in the asymmetric unit of both crystals.
evidence: This is crystallographic data from the structure determination.

claim: DEER measurements were performed at 60 K using a home-built Ku band 17.3 GHz pulse electron spin resonance spectrometer.
